bfbfb670bd: Build00:20–00:55 The major scale formula
149677b364: Whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half
9505c7c1a3: Do Re Mi Fa and Sol La Si Do are each "whole, whole, half", joined by a whole step in the middle. Say it: whole-whole-half, whole, whole-whole-half.
3144aafefb: Start on G and follow the formula, and the seventh note has to be raised a half step to F♯ to fit the "whole, half" ending. That's why G major has one sharp.
99e50740eb: When you run out of fingers, the thumb goes under and the middle finger goes over
3622ac5a98: Right hand going up: after E (finger 3), the thumb passes under the palm to play F and the hand shifts along. Same for the left hand coming down.
649aff814b: Right hand coming down: after the thumb plays F, finger 3 crosses over the thumb to play E. Going up, the left hand's finger 3 crosses over the thumb.
066973ab92: Keep the wrist level as the thumb passes under, without twisting outward; move the thumb to its next spot early so the sound stays connected. Start slow so every crossing is quiet and smooth.
cf7c1d333f: Follow the lit keys and fingering to play C major up and down
d2382c338a: Playing C major up with the right hand, which note does the thumb play after passing under?
bd7b585e8d: 1 2 3 play C D E, the thumb passes under to F, then 2 3 4 5 play G A B C.
6408c8ca5a: In a major scale, which two pairs of neighbouring notes are a half step apart?
1820a999fd: Mi–Fa and Si–Do are a half step apart; every other neighbouring pair is a whole step.

a5328f0955: Hands together: the thumbs pass under at different times
18765ba7dd: Practise the right hand, then the left, and finally put them together. Hands together, the right hand passes under at F and the left crosses over at A, so the two moves are staggered. Start at 50 BPM and add 4 BPM each time it's steady.

8694f805ad: Build00:20–00:55 Four kinds of triad
c96344532f: Major and minor thirds combine into four colours
79effe0ea0: Root, third, fifth: the bottom note is the root and gives the chord its name; the third in the middle decides major or minor; the fifth on top decides augmented or diminished.
607b4b4a9d: Change the root and quality and hear the chord's colour
08cf18d4f6: What notes make up D minor (Dm)?
74d53cb4d2: A minor third D→F, then a major third F→A.
f583c5638b: Lower the third of a C chord, E, by a half step and you get?
a0f0d35ebd: The third decides major or minor: C E G becomes C E♭ G, a C minor triad.
384aceeaf4: BuildThe chord family of C major
06e02cd0c5: Use each note of the scale as a root and stack seven chords
b23773a404: Ⅰ, Ⅳ and Ⅴ are major; Ⅱ, Ⅲ and Ⅵ are minor; Ⅶ is diminished. With white keys alone you can play every chord in C major.

1fb594ae15: Same three notes, a different note at the bottom
1915286b68: Root at the bottom, the most stable. Right-hand fingering 1 3 5.
4bba7b05b9: Third at the bottom, a lighter sound. Right-hand fingering 1 2 5.
723680b84b: Fifth at the bottom, often used to lead into the next chord. Right-hand fingering 1 3 5.
5549a95bc1: Close position: the three notes packed within an octave; open position: the notes spread apart for a wider sound. Lesson 11's tenth accompaniment grows out of open position.
aa50e47d32: Tap an inversion and watch the bottom note change
2d6db0c056: Inversions keep the right hand from moving much and join chords more smoothly
fb34636817: Three arrangements of the same C chord
c40b257a8c: C E G (root at the bottom)
cf6fc56f29: E G C (third at the bottom)
2bbd0d7263: G C E (fifth at the bottom)
f917853f6f: All root position (the hand has to jump)
4982625f7e: C E G (start in root position)
68ba4ca300: C E G (back to root position)
fc6df8c319: Common notes stay put and the others move to the nearest note. This is called "nearest-note voice leading", and nearly every right-hand chord in pop piano is played this way.
8df675b64d: When you invert a chord, its name changes too
80357eefd3: MythThe notes stay the same, so an inverted C chord is still a C chord.
aee957b1d4: The third decides whether a chord is major or minor
6972e7b5f3: FactA major third from root to third makes a major chord; a minor third makes a minor chord.
c2789ed8d8: There are no minor chords in C major
513f33666a: MythDm, Em and Am are all in C major and can be played on white keys alone.
152a15ec28: Augmented and diminished chords both sound uneasy
a090e47c2d: FactBoth contain a dissonant augmented or diminished fifth and are often used to build tension.
f759c667c9: A chord always has to be pressed with three fingers together
5329ce12b5: MythChords can be played apart too; that's the broken-chord accompaniment we start in Lesson 6.
c62c710a3a: The chord symbol C+ means an augmented triad
248a4db41e: FactC+ is the same as Caug; a diminished triad is written C° or Cdim.
